title: Walls and Gates
summary: Fill each empty room with its shortest walking distance to a gate.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–250 rows and 1–250 columns. Input entries are −1, 0, or 2147483647.
contractDetails.callable: `wallsAndGates` returns no value outside R. The judge serializes the mutated input. R returns the updated list.

statement: Fill each empty room with its shortest walking distance to a gate. The integer 2147483647 marks an empty room, −1 marks a wall, and 0 marks a gate. Move through shared edges only. Leave unreachable rooms at 2147483647 and preserve walls and gates. Mutate the supplied grid where the language permits, or return the updated grid in R.

examples.explanation: The two rooms reach different nearest gates.
A wall isolates the empty room.
The upper-left room reaches the gate through the upper-right room.

constraints: 1–250 rows and 1–250 columns. Input entries are −1, 0, or 2147483647.
hints: Conceptual: An empty room's answer may come from any gate.
Directional: Start one BFS queue with all gates at distance zero.
Implementation: When the search first reaches an unfilled room, write the current distance plus one and enqueue it.
complexityAnalysis: O(mn) time and O(mn) auxiliary space for the queue.
